interactions.summary: Jiang restates that Dante's middle-aged lostness is fundamentally a crisis of fear.
A participant reads Virgil's report that Beatrice, moved by love, descended to ask him to rescue Dante from the path where terror turned him aside.
Jiang explains why God would care about Dante at all, leading the room to the answer that Dante's love and poetry raised Beatrice and therefore make Dante a specially reciprocated figure.

claims.claim: The quoted passage says Beatrice intervenes because Dante has been turned aside by terror and because love moves her to speak and descend on his behalf.
Jiang argues that God marks Dante as special because Dante's love and poetry elevate Beatrice to heaven, which gives Beatrice a reason to reciprocate and rescue him.
Jiang treats Dante's continued passion for Beatrice as the one surviving force that distinguishes him even while he is lost in anger, fear, and hatred.

signature_moments.moment: Beatrice's intervention is driven by love itself, not institutional duty.
signature_moments.source_phrase: love prompted me that love which makes me speak
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The line compresses the engine of the rescue into one of the lecture's central causal forces.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says Dante is special because his poetry has already lifted Beatrice to heaven, so heaven must now answer him back.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante is special because he for his poetry is able to elevate Beatrice to heaven
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is a strong Jiang formulation for the reciprocity between love, poetry, and salvation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The heavenly beloved whose love, tears, and reciprocal obligation activate Virgil's intervention.
Jiang uses reciprocal response to explain why Beatrice now helps the poet who once elevated her.
Joined as the mechanism through which Dante matters to heaven and can be singled out for aid.

chronology_notes.note: This packet shifts from Dante's fear to the heavenly chain of intervention that explains why Virgil was sent at all.
